facts.fact: Perth Arena is an entertainment and sports arena in central Perth, Western Australia, used mostly for basketball.
facts.quote: Perth Arena (known commercially as RAC Arena) is an entertainment and sporting arena in the city centre of Perth, Western Australia, used mostly for basketball games.

facts.fact: It was the first stage of Perth City Link, an urban renewal project that sank a railway line to join the city centre to Northbridge.
facts.quote: Perth Arena was the first stage of the Perth City Link, a 13.5-hectare (33-acre) major urban renewal and redevelopment project which involved the sinking of the Eastern Railway to link the Perth central business district directly with Northbridge.

facts.fact: The arena was designed jointly by Ashton Raggatt McDougall and Cameron Chisholm Nicol.
facts.quote: The arena was jointly designed by architectural firms Ashton Raggatt McDougall and Cameron Chisholm Nicol.

facts.fact: Its design is based on the Eternity puzzle, and it seats up to 15,000 for concerts.
facts.quote: With its design based on the Eternity puzzle, the venue holds up to 13,910 spectators for tennis events, 14,846 for basketball (the arena's capacity is capped at 13,000 for National Basketball League regular season games) and a maximum of 15,000 for music or rock concerts.

facts.fact: The arena has a retractable roof, an underground car park, and touring trucks can drive straight onto the floor.
facts.quote: The venue has a retractable roof, 36 luxury appointed corporate suites, a 680-bay underground car park, 5 dedicated function spaces, and touring trucks can drive directly onto the arena floor.

facts.fact: Its cost rose from an estimated $150 million to $550 million during construction.
facts.quote: The construction was marred by controversy in relation to the cost and time blowouts from the original $150 million estimate to $550 million.

facts.fact: The arena opened with an Elton John concert on 10 November 2012.
facts.quote: Elton John opened the arena with a concert on 10 November 2012.

facts.fact: The Palais Garnier is a 1,979-seat opera house on the Place de l'Opéra in Paris.
facts.quote: The Palais Garnier (French: [palɛ ɡaʁnje] , "Garnier Palace"), also known as Opéra Garnier (French: [ɔpeʁa ɡaʁnje] , "Garnier Opera"), is a historic 1,979-seat opera house at the Place de l'Opéra in the 9th arrondissement of Paris, France.

facts.fact: It was built for the Paris Opera from 1861 to 1875 at the wish of Emperor Napoleon III.
facts.quote: It was built for the Paris Opera from 1861 to 1875 at the behest of Emperor Napoleon III.

facts.fact: A design competition for the new opera house was announced on 30 December 1860.
facts.quote: On 30 December 1860 the Second Empire of Emperor Napoleon III officially announced an architectural design competition for the design of the new opera house.

facts.fact: The style mixes Baroque, Palladian classicism and Renaissance elements.
facts.quote: The Napoleon III style was highly eclectic, and borrowed from many historical sources; the opera house included elements from the Baroque, the classicism of Palladio, and Renaissance architecture blended together.

facts.fact: Its structure is masonry walls with hidden iron floors, vaults and roofs.
facts.quote: The structural system is made of masonry walls; concealed iron floors, vaults, and roofs.

facts.fact: The facade uses seventeen different materials, with coloured marble friezes, columns and statues.
facts.quote: The façade of the opera used seventeen different kinds of material, arranged in very elaborate multicolored marble friezes, columns, and lavish statuary, many of which portray deities of Greek mythology.

facts.fact: Inside, corridors, stairs, alcoves and landings let large crowds move and meet during the interval.
facts.quote: The interior consists of interweaving corridors, stairwells, alcoves and landings, allowing the movement of large numbers of people and space for socialising during intermission.

facts.fact: The grand staircase is white marble with a red and green marble balustrade, splitting into two flights up to the Grand Foyer.
facts.quote: The building features a large ceremonial staircase of white marble with a balustrade of red and green marble, which divides into two divergent flights of stairs that lead to the Grand Foyer.

facts.fact: The Secretariat Building is a skyscraper at the United Nations headquarters in Manhattan, holding the offices of the UN Secretariat.
facts.quote: The United Nations Secretariat Building is a skyscraper at the headquarters of the United Nations in the Turtle Bay neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It contains the offices of the United Nations Secretariat, the executive organ of the United Nations (UN).

facts.fact: It was designed in the International Style by ten architects working under Wallace K. Harrison.
facts.quote: The Secretariat Building was designed in the International Style by a team of ten architects working under planning director Wallace K. Harrison.

facts.fact: Harrison chose a design based on the proposals of Oscar Niemeyer and Le Corbusier.
facts.quote: After much discussion, Harrison decided to select a design based on the proposals of two board members, Oscar Niemeyer and Le Corbusier.

facts.fact: It is a rectangular slab; the broad west and east faces are glass curtain walls and the narrow ends are marble.
facts.quote: The Secretariat Building is designed as a rectangular slab measuring 72 by 287 ft (22 by 87 m); it is oriented from north to south and is connected with other UN headquarters buildings. The wider western and eastern elevations of the facade are glass curtain walls, while the narrower northern and southern elevations are made of marble.

facts.fact: It was the first skyscraper in New York City with a glass curtain wall.
facts.quote: The Secretariat Building was the first skyscraper in New York City to use a glass curtain wall.

facts.fact: The blue-green glass was chosen mainly to cut heat on the sunny west face.
facts.quote: The original curtain wall was a single layer of blue-green glass that absorbed heat. The reflective glass was chosen mainly as a means to reduce heat on the western elevation, which absorbed most of the sunlight during a typical workday.

facts.fact: The Vermont marble end walls have no openings and hide the steel frame.
facts.quote: The narrower northern and southern elevations are made of masonry clad with Vermont marble. These elevations rise as unbroken slabs and do not contain any openings.

facts.fact: Staff moved in from August 1950 and the building was completed in June 1951.
facts.quote: Staff started moving into the building on August 21, 1950, and it was completed in June 1951.

facts.fact: The Maisons Jaoul are a pair of houses in Neuilly-sur-Seine, designed by Le Corbusier and built in 1954–56.
facts.quote: Maisons Jaoul are a pair of houses in the upmarket Paris suburb of Neuilly-sur-Seine, designed by Le Corbusier and built in 1954–56.

facts.fact: They are among his key post-war works, with unpainted béton brut concrete and roughly detailed brickwork.
facts.quote: They are among his most important post-war buildings and feature unpainted "béton brut" cast concrete and roughly detailed brickwork.

facts.fact: The houses were drawn in 1937 but built only after the war, for André Jaoul and his son Michel.
facts.quote: The buildings were drawn in 1937 but were only built postwar for André Jaoul and his son Michel.

facts.fact: They have been protected as French historical monuments since 1966.
facts.quote: The Maisons Jaoul have been protected by the French government as historical monuments since 1966, at the request of André Malraux.

facts.fact: These vaulted houses mark a new turn in Le Corbusier's work and can be seen as his first New Brutalist building.
facts.quote: The construction of these vaulted houses signals a new trend in Le Corbusier's work, and the Maisons Jaoul can be considered his first "New Brutalist" work.

facts.fact: The vaults sit on concrete beams that pass their weight to load-bearing brick walls on every side.
facts.quote: These beams in turn transfer the weight to load-bearing brick walls that enclose the houses on every side.

facts.fact: The Port House is the headquarters of the Antwerp Port Authority, built between 2009 and 2016.
facts.quote: The Port Authority Building (Dutch: Havenhuis), or the Port House, is a government building located in Antwerp, Belgium, built between 2009 and 2016.

facts.fact: Designed by Zaha Hadid, it opened in 2016, the year she died, and is her only government building.
facts.quote: Designed by Iraqi-British architect Zaha Hadid, the building opened in 2016, the year of her death. It is the sole government building designed by Hadid.

facts.fact: The lower part was a disused fire station, a protected replica of a Hanseatic house, so it could not be demolished and had to be kept.
facts.quote: The lower section of the building was a disused fire station, and a protected replica of a former Hanseatic house. Thus, it could not be demolished, and the fire station had to be integrated into the new project.

facts.fact: The new glass-covered volume sits directly above the renovated fire station; its glass is meant to reflect the shades of the surrounding water and sky.
facts.quote: The expansion of the building is located directly above the renovated fire station. It has a glass-covered facade to "reflect the complex interaction of shades and colours in the air", a reference to the building's location surrounded by water.

facts.fact: It resembles a ship's hull with a protruding bow, faceted like a diamond, a nod to Antwerp's diamond trade.
facts.quote: The expansion resembles the hull of a sailing ship, with a protruding bow and the surface of the facets of a diamond facing the Kattendijk dock. This is also a reference to Antwerp's association with the diamond industry.

facts.fact: Its triangular facets, some clear and some opaque, let the architects control how much sunlight enters.
facts.quote: The exterior of the "diamond" consists of transparent and opaque triangular facets. This allowed the architects to control the amount of sunlight entering the building.

facts.fact: Concrete pillars and 900 tonnes of steel hold the glass workspace above the fire station.
facts.quote: Project manager Joris Pauwels stated that concrete pillars and 900 tonnes of steel hold the glass workspace above the former fire station.

facts.fact: Designed with energy efficiency in mind, it reached a 'Very Good' BREEAM environmental rating.
facts.quote: The design of the building took energy efficiency into account, reaching a 'Very Good' BREEAM environmental rating.

facts.fact: Torre de Collserola is a tower on Tibidabo hill in Barcelona, designed by Norman Foster with engineers Julio Martínez Calzón and Manuel Julià Vilardell.
facts.quote: Torre de Collserola (Catalan pronunciation: [ˈtorə ðə ˌkɔʎsəˈɾɔlə]) is a uniquely designed tower located on the Tibidabo hill in the Serra de Collserola, in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It was designed by the architect Sir Norman Foster and by the Spanish civil engineers Julio Martínez Calzón and Manuel Julià Vilardell.

facts.fact: It was built in 1991 for the 1992 Summer Olympics.
facts.quote: This emblematic tower was built in 1991 by the construction company Cubiertas y MZOV S.A. for the 1992 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: It has a pod of floors like many towers but is braced by guy wires like a mast.
facts.quote: It features a pod for floor space like many towers but uses guy wires for lateral support like a mast.

facts.fact: The antenna reaches 288.4 m and the thirteen-floor pod tops out at 152 m.
facts.quote: The top antenna reaches 288.4 m (946 ft) and the top of the pod, which has thirteen floors, reaches 152 m (499 ft).

facts.fact: Its slip-formed reinforced concrete shaft is only 4.5 m across.
facts.quote: The tower has a hollow slip-formed, reinforced concrete main shaft of only 4.5 m diameter, which reduces to a mere 3 m to hold a radio mast which telescopes from 2.7 m to 0.7 m.

facts.fact: The floors are wrapped in open stainless steel grilles and hung from the shaft by three steel trusses.
facts.quote: The thirteen floors are surrounded by a perimeter of open stainless steel grilles and suspended from the shaft by three primary vertical steel trusses.

facts.fact: The upper guy cables are made of aramid fibre.
facts.quote: The upper guys are made of three series of 7 aramid fibre cables in parallel (56 mm diameter), each terminated with a resin socket.

facts.fact: The tenth floor of the pod is open to the public.
facts.quote: The tenth floor of the pod is open to the public.

facts.fact: The Miho Museum is an art museum southeast of Kyoto, in Kōka, Shiga Prefecture.
facts.quote: The Miho Museum (Japanese: ミホ ミュージアム, romanized: Miho myūjiamu) is an art museum located southeast of Kyoto, Japan, in the Shigaraki neighborhood of the city of Kōka, in Shiga Prefecture.

facts.fact: Mihoko Koyama and her daughter Hiroko commissioned I. M. Pei to design it.
facts.quote: Mihoko Koyama and her daughter, Hiroko Koyama, commissioned the American architect I. M. Pei to design the Miho Museum.

facts.fact: Pei called the design Shangri-La; it sits in a hilly, forested landscape.
facts.quote: Pei's design, which he came to call Shangri-La, is executed in a hilly and forested landscape.

facts.fact: About three-quarters of the 17,400 m² building is underground, carved out of a rocky mountaintop.
facts.quote: Approximately three-quarters of the 17,400 square meter building is situated underground, carved out of a rocky mountaintop.

facts.fact: The roof is glass and steel; walls and floors are a beige French limestone also used at the Louvre's reception hall.
facts.quote: The roof is a large glass and steel construction, while the exterior and interior walls and floor are made of a warm beige-colored limestone from France – the same material used by Pei in the reception hall of the Louvre.

facts.fact: Pei kept changing the galleries during construction as new pieces joined the collection.
facts.quote: Pei continued to make changes to the design of the galleries during construction as new pieces were acquired for the collection.

facts.fact: The museum opened in 1997.
facts.quote: Since its opening in 1997, the museum has been run by the Shumei Cultural Foundation.

facts.fact: The Fernsehturm in central Berlin was built in 1965–69 by the East German government as a broadcasting tower and a symbol of communist power.
facts.quote: The Fernsehturm (German: [ˈfɛɐ̯nzeːˌtʊɐ̯m] ; lit. 'Television Tower') in central Berlin was constructed between 1965 and 1969 by the government of the German Democratic Republic as both a functional broadcasting facility and a symbol of communist power.

facts.fact: At 368 metres including its antenna, it is the tallest structure in Germany.
facts.quote: With a height of 368 metres (1,207 ft) (including antenna) it is the tallest structure in Germany, and the third-tallest structure in the European Union.

facts.fact: Walter Ulbricht allowed a tower modelled on the Fernsehturm Stuttgart and on the Sputnik satellite.
facts.quote: Walter Ulbricht, leader of the Socialist Unity Party which governed East Germany, decided to allow the construction of a television tower modelled on the Fernsehturm Stuttgart and the first artificial Earth satellite, Sputnik.

facts.fact: Several architects worked on it, including Hermann Henselmann, Fritz Dieter and Günter Franke.
facts.quote: Various architects were involved in the planning and implementation of the tower between 1965 and 1969, including Hermann Henselmann and Jörg Streitparth, Fritz Dieter, Günter Franke and Werner Ahrendt, as well as Walter Herzog, Gerhard Kosel and Herbert Aust.

facts.fact: The concrete shaft is 248.78 metres high and used 8,000 cubic metres of concrete.
facts.quote: A total of 8,000 cubic metres (10,000 cu. yd.) of concrete was used to build the shaft, which was 248.78 metres (816.2 ft) high and weighed 26,000 tons.

facts.fact: The ball was assembled from 120 separate segments, pre-assembled on the ground.
facts.quote: The working group VEB Ipro had worked out the procedure for assembling the ball on the reinforced concrete shaft, according to which the ball could be pieced together from 120 separate segments on the ground.

facts.fact: The sphere holds a visitor platform and a revolving restaurant.
facts.quote: The sphere is a visitor platform and a revolving restaurant in the middle of the sphere.

facts.fact: Sunlight on the tiled stainless-steel dome usually reflects as a cross, nicknamed the 'Pope's Revenge'.
facts.quote: When the sun shines on the Fernsehturm's tiled stainless-steel dome, the reflection usually appears in the form of a Greek cross. Berliners nicknamed the luminous cross Rache des Papstes, or the "Pope's Revenge", believing the Christian symbol a divine retaliation for the government's removal of crosses from East Berlin's churches.

facts.fact: It has been a listed monument since 1979.
facts.quote: In 1979, the Berlin TV Tower received official monument status by the East German government, a status which was perpetuated after the German reunification.

facts.fact: NEMO Science Museum is a science centre in Amsterdam.
facts.quote: NEMO Science Museum (from Latin: Nemo, lit. 'Nobody') is a science centre in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.fact: Since 1997 it has been housed in a building designed by Renzo Piano.
facts.quote: The museum has its origins in 1923, and is housed in a building designed by Renzo Piano since 1997.

facts.fact: It holds five floors of hands-on science exhibitions and is the largest science centre in the Netherlands.
facts.quote: It contains five floors of hands-on science exhibitions and is the largest science center in the Netherlands.

facts.fact: Piano's building, first called New Metropolis, stands at the edge of the harbour and looks like the hull of an enormous ship.
facts.quote: His other projects begun in the 1990s included the New Metropolis Museum in Amsterdam, which later became the science museum and technology NEMO (1992–1997), placed on the edge of the harbor, and resembling the hull of an enormous ship; the Parco della Musica, a complex of music performance halls in Rome (1994–2002), Each was entirely different from the others, and in this period it was difficult to discern a specific element that or style defined his architecture, other than careful craftsmanship and attention to detail.

facts.fact: The top level, an upper deck, has a café, a children's play area and a wide view of the city.
facts.quote: The fifth floor or upper deck has a cafeteria, a children's play area and a great view of the city surroundings.

facts.fact: The Museum für Moderne Kunst (MMK) in Frankfurt was founded in 1981 and opened on 6 June 1991.
facts.quote: The Museum für Moderne Kunst (Museum of Modern Art), or short MMK, in Frankfurt, was founded in 1981 and opened to the public 6 June 1991.

facts.fact: Hans Hollein won the competition for the museum in 1983.
facts.quote: In 1983, Hollein won the competition for the Museum für Moderne Kunst; three years earlier, his proposal for the city's Museum für angewandte Kunst had finished a close second behind Richard Meier's prize-winning design.

facts.fact: Because of its triangular shape, it is popularly called the 'piece of cake'.
facts.quote: Because of its triangular shape, the MMK is popularly called the Tortenstück ("piece of cake").

facts.fact: Hollein shaped the building to its three-sided site, so the large rooms at the narrow end are wedge-shaped; there are 3,500 m² of galleries.
facts.quote: Hollein molded a building to the three-sided space, so that the large rooms at the narrow end are wedge-shaped, producing 3,500 m2 (38,000 ft2) of exhibition space.

facts.fact: The three-storey building's height is matched to its surroundings.
facts.quote: The height of the three-storey building is adapted to the surroundings and is characterised by the "triangular shape" and facade design.

facts.fact: It has three main exhibition levels, with offices on a mezzanine above the entrance and café.
facts.quote: The building houses three main levels for exhibitions and an administration area on the mezzanine, which is located above the entrance area and the cafeteria.

facts.fact: Work began in 1987 and the museum cost about $38 million.
facts.quote: The ground-breaking was delayed until 1987, and the new museum was eventually built at a cost of about $38 million.

facts.fact: Immeuble Clarté is an apartment building in Geneva by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret, designed from 1928 and built in 1931–32.
facts.quote: Immeuble Clarté is an apartment building in Geneva designed by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret starting from 1928 and built in 1931–32.

facts.fact: It has eight storeys with 45 free-plan flats of different layouts and sizes.
facts.quote: It has eight stories comprising 45 free plan units of diverse configurations and sizes.

facts.fact: It is a key early project in which Le Corbusier tested modernist ideas for apartment buildings, later leading to the Unité d'Habitation.
facts.quote: It is one of Le Corbusier's key early projects in which he explored the principles of modernist architecture in apartment buildings, which later led to the Unité d'Habitation design principle.

facts.fact: After threats of demolition, it was listed as a historic monument in 1986.
facts.quote: After being again threatened with demolition in the early 1980s, in 1986 it was listed as a historic monument.

facts.fact: In 2016 it became part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing of Le Corbusier's works.
facts.quote: In July 2016, the building and several other works by Le Corbusier were inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

facts.fact: The Pinakothek der Moderne is a modern art museum in Munich's Kunstareal.
facts.quote: The Pinakothek der Moderne (German: [pinakoˈteːk deːɐ̯ moˈdɛʁnə], Pinakothek of the Modern) is a modern art museum, situated in central Munich's Kunstareal.

facts.fact: Designed by Stephan Braunfels, it opened in September 2002 after seven years of construction.
facts.quote: Designed by German architect Stephan Braunfels, the Pinakothek der Moderne was inaugurated in September 2002 after seven years of construction.

facts.fact: Braunfels won the competition for it in 1992.
facts.quote: The first major competition he won was for Munich's Pinakothek der Moderne in 1992.

facts.fact: Its straight facade of white and grey concrete is broken by large windows and tall columns carrying a wide canopy roof.
facts.quote: The rectilinear facade, dominated by white and grey concrete, is interrupted by large windows and high rise columns, the latter supporting the extensive canopied roof.

facts.fact: A central domed rotunda links the four corners, each given to one collection: art, architecture, design and works on paper.
facts.quote: Each of the four corners of the building, connected by a central domed rotunda, is dedicated to a special collection. The Museum is thus divided into Art (Kunst), Architecture (Architektur), Design (Design) and Works on Paper (Graphik).

facts.fact: The art floor is lit from above by daylight, helped by computer-controlled lamps for even, almost shadowless light.
facts.quote: The first floor, containing the art collection, has ample natural light from above, augmented by computer-controlled lamps, designed to keep a consistent, nearly shadowless illumination against the gray floors and white walls.

facts.fact: The project took ten years and opened in late 2002 as one of the largest new museums in Germany.
facts.quote: This project took ten years to come to fruition and opened in late 2002 as one of the largest new museums in Germany.

facts.fact: The Weisman Art Museum is the art museum of the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis.
facts.quote: Weisman Art Museum is an art museum at the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

facts.fact: In 1993 the museum moved into its present building by Frank Gehry and was named after collector Frederick R. Weisman.
facts.quote: In 1993, the museum moved to its current building, designed by the Canadian-born American architect Frank Gehry, and renamed in honor of art collector and philanthropist Frederick R. Weisman.

facts.fact: Gehry designed it with MSR Design as architect of record; it was completed in November 1993.
facts.quote: The current museum building was designed by architect Frank Gehry with MSR Design as architect of record and completed in November 1993.

facts.fact: It stands on a bluff above the Mississippi River at the east end of the Washington Avenue Bridge.
facts.quote: It is one of the major landmarks on the University of Minnesota campus, situated on a bluff overlooking the Mississippi River at the east end of the Washington Avenue Bridge.

facts.fact: It is considered significant because it was built before computer-aided design was widely used in architecture.
facts.quote: The abstract structure is considered highly significant because it was built prior to the widespread use of computer aided design in architecture.

facts.fact: It shows two faces: brick to the south and east, matching the historic buildings on Northrop Mall.
facts.quote: The building presents two faces, depending on which side it is viewed from. To the south and east, it presents a brick facade that blends with the historic buildings along Northrop Mall.

facts.fact: To the north and west it becomes an abstract fish and waterfall of curved and angular brushed steel sheets.
facts.quote: To the north and west, it is an abstraction of a fish and waterfall in curving and angular brushed steel sheets.

facts.fact: Gehry also designed a major addition, completed in 2011.
facts.quote: The museum received a major addition, also designed by Frank Gehry, in 2011.

facts.fact: Soreq Nuclear Research Center is a research institute near Palmachim and Yavne in Israel.
facts.quote: Soreq Nuclear Research Center is a research and development institute situated near the localities of Palmachim and Yavne in Israel.

facts.fact: Its research facilities include a 5 MW pool-type research reactor supplied from the United States in the late 1950s.
facts.quote: Some of the institute's research facilities include an AMF 5 MW pool-type light water nuclear reactor supplied in the late 1950s from the United States under the Atoms for Peace program and a 10 MeV proton cyclotron accelerator, as well as extensive laboratory and testing facilities.

facts.fact: Philip Johnson designed the center's building in 1956; it was his first government commission.
facts.quote: Noted American modernist architect Philip Johnson designed the center's building in 1956. The project was Johnson's first government commission.

facts.fact: Structural engineer Lev Zetlin worked closely with Johnson on the design and construction of the reactor.
facts.quote: Zetlin, one of the most renowned practitioners of his profession, worked very closely with Johnson in the design and construction of the reactor.

facts.fact: Johnson never visited the site and called it "my temple in the desert".
facts.quote: Johnson, who never visited the site, called it "my temple in the desert."

facts.fact: Kunsten was built in 1968–72 by Elissa and Alvar Aalto with Danish architect Jean-Jacques Baruël.
facts.quote: Of a modern Scandinavian design, it was built between 1968 and 1972 by Finnish architects Elissa and Alvar Aalto and Danish architect Jean-Jacques Baruël.

facts.fact: The design was chosen from 144 entries to a Nordic architectural competition.
facts.quote: The architectural plans for designing the museum were selected from the 144 submissions made to the Nordic architectural competition by 15 January 1958.

facts.fact: It rises against the hills like a ziggurat and covers over 6,000 m².
facts.quote: The museum, rising against the hills like a ziggurat, extends over 6,000 m2 (65,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: It has a square plan, with ground-floor galleries around a central exhibition hall.
facts.quote: It is built to a square plan with galleries organised on the ground level around the central exhibition area.

facts.fact: Skylights, reflectors and light-coloured materials shape the Nordic light in the galleries.
facts.quote: The combination of strategically placed skylights and diffused lighting has effectively "manipulated the Nordic light" in illuminating the galleries, relying on a series of reflectors and light-coloured materials.

facts.fact: The long skylights limit sun on the south side to 56 degrees and open fully to the north.
facts.quote: The "two-sided, elongated skylights" control the sunlight on the southern side to a restricted angle of 56 degrees whereas it is fully open at a 90-degree angle on its northern side.

facts.fact: The outside is marble, glass, wood and copper sheet; most floors are Carrara marble.
facts.quote: The external facade is made of marble, glass, wood, and copper sheeting. Most of the interior floor space and pavement are of Carrara marble.

facts.fact: The grounds include a sculpture park, an amphitheatre and a terrace.
facts.quote: The surrounding outdoor areas include a well-tended sculpture park, an amphitheatre and a terrace.

facts.fact: The building in downtown New Haven is the headquarters of the Knights of Columbus.
facts.quote: The Knights of Columbus Building, in Downtown New Haven, Connecticut, is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic fraternal service organization, the Knights of Columbus.

facts.fact: It was designed by Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates and finished in 1969.
facts.quote: Also known as the Knights of Columbus Tower or The Knights' Tower, the building was designed by Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates and finished in 1969.

facts.fact: It is a 23-storey reinforced concrete building, 98 metres tall.
facts.quote: This 23-story modern style reinforced concrete building, at 320 feet (98 meters) tall, is the third-tallest building in the city's skyline.

facts.fact: The round corner towers give it a simple geometric form and stand for the Order's four principles.
facts.quote: The cylindrical towers at the corners give the structure a simple geometric form and represent the four core principles of the Order: Charity, Unity, Fraternity, and Patriotism.

facts.fact: Locally it is called the "Tootsie Roll Building" because of its corner towers.
facts.quote: Locally the building is also known as the "Tootsie Roll Building" due to its distinctive corner towers.

facts.fact: It stood next to the New Haven Coliseum, by the same firm, demolished in 2007.
facts.quote: The building was built at 1 Columbus Plaza next to the New Haven Coliseum (razed in 2007), which was designed by the same firm.

facts.fact: The Natural History Museum in London shows a vast range of natural history specimens.
facts.quote: The Natural History Museum in London, England, is a museum that exhibits a vast range of specimens from various segments of natural history.

facts.fact: Captain Francis Fowke won the 1864 design competition but died in December 1865.
facts.quote: The winning entry was submitted by the civil engineer Captain Francis Fowke, who died shortly afterwards in December 1865.

facts.fact: Alfred Waterhouse took over in 1866, revised the plans and designed the facades in his own Romanesque style.
facts.quote: The scheme was taken over by Alfred Waterhouse, who was hired in February 1866, and who substantially revised the agreed plans, and designed the façades in his own idiosyncratic Romanesque style, which was inspired by his frequent visits to the Continent.

facts.fact: Building work ran from 1873 to 1880.
facts.quote: Work began in 1873 and was completed in 1880.

facts.fact: Inside and out, the building uses terracotta tiles to resist the sooty air of Victorian London.
facts.quote: Both the interiors and exteriors of the Waterhouse building make extensive use of architectural terracotta tiles to resist the sooty atmosphere of Victorian London, manufactured by the Tamworth-based company of Gibbs and Canning.

facts.fact: The tiles carry reliefs of plants and animals: living species in the west wing, extinct ones in the east.
facts.quote: The tiles and bricks feature many relief sculptures of flora and fauna, with living and extinct species featured within the west and east wings respectively.

facts.fact: Its ornate architecture is sometimes called a cathedral of nature; a blue whale skeleton now hangs in the vaulted central hall.
facts.quote: The museum is particularly famous for its exhibition of dinosaur skeletons and ornate architecture—sometimes dubbed a cathedral of nature—both exemplified by the large Diplodocus cast that dominated the vaulted central hall before it was replaced in 2017 with the skeleton of a blue whale hanging from the ceiling.

facts.fact: Its central axis lines up with the Imperial College tower, the Royal Albert Hall and the Albert Memorial.
facts.quote: The central axis of the museum is aligned with the tower of Imperial College London (formerly the Imperial Institute) and the Royal Albert Hall and Albert Memorial further north.

facts.fact: 28 Liberty Street, formerly One Chase Manhattan Plaza, is a 60-storey International Style skyscraper in Manhattan's Financial District.
facts.quote: 28 Liberty Street, formerly known as One Chase Manhattan Plaza, is a 60-story International Style skyscraper between Nassau, Liberty, William, and Pine Streets in the Financial District of Manhattan in New York City.

facts.fact: Designed by Gordon Bunshaft of SOM, it opened in 1961 and is 248 metres tall.
facts.quote: The building, designed by Gordon Bunshaft of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), opened in 1961. It is 813 feet (248 m) tall.

facts.fact: The tower covers only about 28 percent of its site.
facts.quote: 28 Liberty Street occupies only about 28 percent of its 2.5-acre (1.0 ha) site.

facts.fact: Its plaza holds a sunken Japanese rock garden by Isamu Noguchi.
facts.quote: The tower is surrounded by a plaza that contains a sunken Japanese rock garden, designed by Isamu Noguchi, to the south.

facts.fact: The columns stand out from the building on its long sides, while the floors cantilever from them at the short ends.
facts.quote: The columns extend from the building on its long sides, while the floors cantilever from the columns on the building's short dimensions.

facts.fact: At ground level the columns form a colonnade around the recessed lobby.
facts.quote: The presence of the columns at ground level creates a colonnade around the lobby, which is recessed behind the upper floors.

facts.fact: The glass is set in aluminium panels and mullions, chosen for durability.
facts.quote: The glass panes are set within aluminum panels (chosen for their durability and performance) as well as vertical aluminum mullions.

facts.fact: It was designated a New York City landmark in 2008.
facts.quote: The New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the building a landmark in 2008.

facts.fact: Isozaki's Kitakyushu Central Library (1973–74) belongs to the period when his style was still evolving.
facts.quote: His style continued to evolve with buildings such as the Fujimi Country Club (1973–74) and Kitakyushu Central Library (1973–74).

facts.fact: The Mole Antonelliana is a landmark in Turin named after its architect, Alessandro Antonelli.
facts.quote: The Mole Antonelliana (pronounced [ˈmɔːle antonelˈljaːna]) is a major landmark building in Turin, Italy, named after its architect, Alessandro Antonelli.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1863 and was completed in 1889, after the architect's death.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1863, soon after Italian unification, and was completed in 1889, after the architect's death.

facts.fact: It was first conceived as a synagogue and now houses the National Museum of Cinema.
facts.quote: Originally conceived of as a synagogue, it now houses the National Museum of Cinema, and is believed to be the tallest museum in the world.

facts.fact: Antonelli kept changing the design, raising its height to 167.5 metres.
facts.quote: He proposed a series of modifications which raised the final height to 167.5 m (550 ft), over 46 m (151 ft) higher than the dome in the original design.

facts.fact: The people of Turin asked the city to take over the unfinished building, and it did.
facts.quote: The people of Turin, who had watched the synagogue rise skyward, demanded that the city take over the project, which it did.

facts.fact: It is the tallest unreinforced brick building in the world, built without a steel skeleton.
facts.quote: The Mole Antonelliana is the tallest unreinforced brick building in the world (built without a steel girder skeleton).

facts.fact: Catalan vaults, rare in Italy, form the ceiling of the ground floor under the atrium.
facts.quote: Catalan vaults are featured in the ceiling of the ground floor under the atrium, which are relatively rare in Italy but popular in Spain, where they originated.

facts.fact: A storm in 1953 destroyed the top 47 metres of the spire, rebuilt in 1961 as a stone-faced metal structure.
facts.quote: On 23 May 1953, a violent cloudburst, accompanied by a tornado, destroyed the uppermost 47 m (154 ft) of the pinnacle, which was rebuilt in 1961 as a metal structure faced with stone.

facts.fact: The museum is the Smithsonian's museum of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas.
facts.quote: The National Museum of the American Indian is a museum in the United States devoted to the culture of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas. It is part of the Smithsonian Institution group of museums and research centers.

facts.fact: Its building on the National Mall opened on 21 September 2004, the first national museum in the US dedicated only to Native Americans.
facts.quote: The museum opened on September 21, 2004. Fifteen years in the making, it was the first national museum in the country dedicated exclusively to Native Americans.

facts.fact: The five-storey curving building is clad in golden Kasota limestone meant to evoke rock shaped by wind and water.
facts.quote: The five-story, 250,000-square-foot (23,000 m2), curvilinear building is clad in a golden-colored Kasota limestone designed to evoke natural rock formations shaped by wind and water over thousands of years.

facts.fact: The site is surrounded by simulated wetlands.
facts.quote: The museum is set in a 4.25 acres (17,200 m2)-site and is surrounded by simulated wetlands.

facts.fact: The east-facing entrance, prism window and 37-metre-high performance space came from consultations with Native peoples.
facts.quote: The museum's east-facing entrance, its prism window and its 120-foot (37 m) high space for contemporary Native performances are direct results of extensive consultations with Native peoples.

facts.fact: Douglas Cardinal (Blackfoot) is the architect; GBQC Architects and Johnpaul Jones were design architects.
facts.quote: The museum's architect and project designer is Canadian Douglas Cardinal (Blackfoot); its design architects are GBQC Architects of Philadelphia and architect Johnpaul Jones (Cherokee/Choctaw).

facts.fact: Cardinal was removed during construction, but the building keeps his original design intent.
facts.quote: Disagreements during construction led to Cardinal's being removed from the project, but the building retains his original design intent.

facts.fact: Inside, the walls are mostly curved, with almost no sharp corners.
facts.quote: This theme of organic flow is reflected by the interior of the museum, whose walls are mostly curving surfaces, with almost no sharp corners.

facts.fact: The Pinacoteca Agnelli is an art gallery in Turin.
facts.quote: The Pinacoteca Giovanni e Marella Agnelli or Pinacoteca Agnelli is an art gallery in Turin, Italy.

facts.fact: It opened in 2002 on the top floor of the Lingotto complex, headquarters of the carmaker Fiat.
facts.quote: It opened in 2002 on the top floor of the Lingotto complex, the headquarters of the Italian auto giant Fiat S.p.A. founded in 1899 by Giovanni Agnelli.

facts.fact: Its 'Lo scrigno', a 450 m² steel structure by Renzo Piano, is raised 34 metres above the rooftop test track.
facts.quote: As part of the complex, Lo scrigno, a 450 square-metre steel structure designed by Renzo Piano, is raised 34 metres off the test track on the roof of the plant.

facts.fact: Its style suggests a crystal spaceship, echoing the futuristic original building.
facts.quote: Its style represents a crystal spaceship, referring back to the original building's futuristic style.

facts.fact: The collection comes from Gianni and Marella Agnelli's private collection, including Renoir and Manet.
facts.quote: Its permanent collection is a selection of paintings and sculptures from Gianni and Marella Agnelli's private collection, such as Pierre-Auguste Renoir's Blonde Bather and Édouard Manet's La Négresse, as well as paintings by Henri Matisse, Canaletto, Giovanni Battista Tiepolo, Antonio Canova, Pablo Picasso, and Amedeo Modigliani.

facts.fact: The building in Ginza, Tokyo, built in 1967, is considered the first realisation of Kenzo Tange's Metabolist ideas.
facts.quote: The Shizuoka Press and Broadcasting Center is a building located in Ginza, Tokyo, Japan. Built in 1967, it is considered to be the first realization of Kenzo Tange's Metabolist movement, which called for a new urban typology that could self-perpetuate in an organic, "metabolic" way.

facts.fact: On a small triangular site, thirteen offices hang asymmetrically from a single round core 7.7 metres across.
facts.quote: It was built on a 189 square metres (2,030 sq ft) triangular site, and erected around a column, 7.7 metres (25 ft) in diameter, which forms the building's central core, and around which thirteen individual offices are connected asymmetrically.

facts.fact: It was meant as a prototype for a prefabricated urban megastructure that could keep renewing itself.
facts.quote: The building was meant to be a prototype for a perpetually regenerating, prefabricated urban megastructure.

facts.fact: The gaps between office clusters were meant to be filled with more offices later, but this never happened.
facts.quote: It was designed with the intention that the space between the office clusters could be filled with additional offices in the future as demand increased. However, this idea was never realized and the building remains unchanged since it was built.

facts.fact: The offices are cantilevered steel and glass boxes around one core.
facts.quote: This time using only a single core Tange arranged the offices as cantilevered steel and glass boxes.

facts.fact: The concrete was cast in aluminium formwork, which was left on as cladding.
facts.quote: The concrete forms of the building were cast using aluminium formwork and the aluminium has been left on as a cladding.

facts.fact: The McLaren Technology Centre is the headquarters of the McLaren Group in Woking, Surrey.
facts.quote: The McLaren Technology Centre (MTC) is the headquarters of the McLaren Group and its subsidiaries, located on a 500,000 m2 (50 ha) site in Woking, Surrey, England.

facts.fact: The main building is a roughly semicircular, glass-walled building by Foster + Partners.
facts.quote: The main building is a large, roughly semi-circular, glass-walled building, designed by architect Norman Foster and his company, Foster + Partners.

facts.fact: It was shortlisted for the 2005 Stirling Prize.
facts.quote: The building was short-listed for the 2005 Stirling Prize, which was won by the Scottish Parliament building.

facts.fact: A formal lake completes the circle of the building, with four further 'ecology' lakes.
facts.quote: The building is accompanied by a series of artificial lakes: one formal lake directly opposite that completes the circle of the building, and a further four 'ecology' lakes.

facts.fact: Lake water is pumped through heat exchangers to cool the building and the wind tunnels.
facts.quote: This water is pumped through a series of heat exchangers to cool the building and to dissipate the heat produced by the wind tunnels.

facts.fact: Work space is split into 18-metre 'fingers' separated by 6-metre corridors called 'streets'.
facts.quote: The main working space of the building is split into 18 metre wide sections known as 'fingers' that are separated by six-metre-wide (20 ft) corridors known as 'streets'.

facts.fact: It brought together McLaren's work from 18 separate sites.
facts.quote: The Technology Centre consolidated all aspects of the McLaren Group at one site, instead of the 18 separate sites previously occupied.

facts.fact: McLaren staff started using the building in May 2003.
facts.quote: McLaren employees started using the facility in May 2003.

facts.fact: Tange was commissioned in 1961; the centre in Kōfu was completed in 1966 as headquarters of the Yamanashi Broadcasting System, with radio and TV studios and newspaper presses.
facts.quote: Tange was commissioned to build a communications centre in Kōfu in 1961. In 1966, the Yamanashi Press and Broadcasting Centre, a building which would serve as the headquarters for the Yamanashi Broadcasting System and house several of its divisions, including studios for radio and television and printing presses for a newspaper, was completed.

facts.fact: It was one of Tange's few chances to build his Metabolist ideas of movement and growth, at a small scale.
facts.quote: The Press and Broadcasting Centre was one of the few opportunities Tange had to fully implement his Metabolist ideals of constant movement and expansion, albeit at a small scale.

facts.fact: It grows from sixteen towers, each five metres across but of different heights, carrying stairs, lifts and services, spanned by large floor trays.
facts.quote: The building grows out of sixteen towers, all five metres in diameter but varying in height, which carry vertical circulation and services including stairs and lifts. They are spanned by large, horizontal floor trays, which house the activities performed in the building.

facts.fact: Some floor plates were left out to allow growth; these gaps have since become gardens.
facts.quote: The plan of the building emphasised possibilities for continuous modification and growth by omitting some floor plates, which have since been filled in with gardens, and by the possibility for modifications around the sixteen towers which house essential circulation and services.

facts.fact: The printing plant is on the ground floor for easy street access for loading.
facts.quote: He stacked these functions vertically according to need, for example, the printing plant is on the ground floor to facilitate access to the street for loading and transportation.

facts.fact: Tange left the towers at different heights to suggest room to grow upward.
facts.quote: Tange deliberately finished the cylindrical towers at different heights to imply that there was room for vertical expansion.

facts.fact: Mode Gakuen Cocoon Tower is a 204-metre, 50-storey school building in Nishi-Shinjuku, Tokyo.
facts.quote: Mode Gakuen Cocoon Tower (モード学園コクーンタワー, Mōdo gakuen kokūn tawā) is a 204-metre-tall (669-foot), 50-story educational facility located in the Nishi-Shinjuku district in Shinjuku, Tokyo, Japan.

facts.fact: It was designed by a team led by Paul Noritaka Tange, son of Kenzo Tange.
facts.quote: The building was designed by a team led by Paul Noritaka Tange, the son of Kenzo Tange.

facts.fact: The competition brief said the building could not be rectangular.
facts.quote: Mode Gakuen invited architects to compete to build its new Tokyo location, stipulating that the building could not be rectangular.

facts.fact: The winning design is a curved shell of white aluminium and dark blue glass, crossed by a web of white diagonals.
facts.quote: The winner had a curved shell of white aluminum and dark blue glass, criss-crossed by a web of white diagonal lines.

facts.fact: Its cocoon shape symbolises nurturing the students inside.
facts.quote: The architects, Tange Associates, said its cocoon-like shape symbolizes nurturing the students inside; they also said they wanted the building to revitalize the surrounding area and to create a gateway between Shinjuku Station and the Shinjuku central business district.

facts.fact: Each floor has three rectangular classrooms around a core of lift, stairs and support shaft.
facts.quote: Each floor of the tower contains three rectangular classrooms that surround an inner core. The inner core consists of an elevator, a staircase and a support shaft.

facts.fact: Every three floors, a three-storey student lounge sits between the classrooms.
facts.quote: Every three floors, a three-story student lounge is located between the classrooms and faces three directions: east, southwest and northwest.

facts.fact: It won Emporis's 2008 Skyscraper of the Year award.
facts.quote: It was awarded the 2008 Skyscraper of the Year by Emporis.

facts.fact: Palazzo Lombardia is an office complex in Milan with a 43-storey, 161-metre tower.
facts.quote: Palazzo Lombardia ("Lombardy Building") is an office complex in Milan, Italy, including a 43-storey, 161 m (528 ft) tall skyscraper.

facts.fact: It is the main seat of the Lombardy regional government.
facts.quote: It is the main seat of the Lombardy regional government, located in the Centro Direzionale di Milano (CBD, Central Business District), north-west of the city centre.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated in January 2010 and completed in March 2010.
facts.quote: It was first inaugurated on 22 January 2010, and officially completed on 21 March 2010.

facts.fact: When completed it was briefly the tallest skyscraper in Italy.
facts.quote: After its completion, the Regione Lombardia skyscraper was briefly the tallest skyscraper both in Milan and in Italy, being taller than both the Telecom Italia Tower in Naples and the Pirelli Tower in Milan.

facts.fact: Pei Cobb Freed & Partners won the 2004 international competition, with Henry N. Cobb as design partner.
facts.quote: Palazzo Lombardia was designed by the architectural firm Pei Cobb Freed & Partners, winner of an international design competition in 2004, with Henry N. Cobb as design partner.

facts.fact: It won the 2012 International Architecture Award.
facts.quote: The building won the 2012 International Architecture Award for the best new global design.

facts.fact: Tokyo Tower is a communications and observation tower in Minato, Tokyo, completed in 1958.
facts.quote: Tokyo Tower (東京タワー, Tōkyō Tawā; pronounced [toːkʲoː taꜜɰᵝaː] ), also known by its official name Japan Radio Tower (日本電波塔, Nippon denpatō) is a communications and observation tower in the district of Shiba-koen in Minato, Tokyo, Japan, completed in 1958.

facts.fact: It is a lattice tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower, painted white and international orange for air safety.
facts.quote: It is a lattice tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower, and is painted white and international orange to comply with air safety regulations.

facts.fact: Tachū Naitō was chosen to design it and based his design on the Eiffel Tower.
facts.quote: Tachū Naitō, designer of tall buildings in Japan, was chosen to design the newly proposed tower. Looking to the Western world for inspiration, Naitō based his design on the Eiffel Tower in Paris, France.

facts.fact: With Nikken Sekkei, Naitō claimed it could withstand earthquakes twice as strong as the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake.
facts.quote: With the help of engineering company Nikken Sekkei Ltd., Naitō claimed his design could withstand earthquakes with twice the intensity of the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake or typhoons with wind speeds of up to 220 km/h (140 mph).

facts.fact: It is steel, a third of it scrap from US tanks damaged in the Korean War.
facts.quote: It was constructed of steel, a third of which was scrap metal taken from US tanks damaged in the Korean War.

facts.fact: At 332.9 metres it was Japan's tallest tower until Tokyo Skytree in 2012.
facts.quote: At 332.9 meters (1,092 feet), it was the tallest tower in Japan until the construction of Tokyo Skytree in 2012.

facts.fact: Taller than the Eiffel Tower, it weighs about 4,000 tons, far less, being thinner and simpler.
facts.quote: Though physically taller than the Eiffel Tower, Tokyo Tower weighs about 4,000 tons, 3,300 less than the Eiffel Tower as it is significantly thinner and simpler in construction.

facts.fact: Visitors can go up to a two-storey Main Deck at 150 m and a Top Deck at 249.6 m.
facts.quote: Departing from it, guests can visit two observation decks: the two-story Main Deck at 150 m (490 ft), and the smaller Top Deck at 249.6 m (819 ft).

facts.fact: Torre Emperador, formerly Torre Espacio, is a 230-metre, 57-floor office skyscraper in Madrid.
facts.quote: The Torre Emperador Castellana, simply known as Torre Emperador and formerly named Torre Espacio (Spanish for Space Tower), is an office skyscraper in Madrid, Spain, standing at 230 m (750 ft) tall and containing 57 floors.

facts.fact: It was designed by Henry N. Cobb of Pei Cobb Freed and built by OHL.
facts.quote: It was designed by American architect Henry N. Cobb, a partner in the firm Pei Cobb Freed, and built by OHL.

facts.fact: It was topped out on 19 March 2007.
facts.quote: The structure was topped out on 19 March 2007.

facts.fact: At 230 metres it became, for a time, the tallest structure in Spain.
facts.quote: With its 230 m, it also became the tallest structure in Spain at that time, surpassing the telecommunications tower Torrespaña.

facts.fact: Its unusual form led to a feature on the Discovery Channel's Build It Bigger.
facts.quote: The building project was featured on the Discovery Channel's Build It Bigger series due to the skyscraper's unique form and shape.

facts.fact: Since 2009 it has housed the British Embassy in Madrid.
facts.quote: In 2009, it became the new home of the British Embassy in Madrid.

facts.fact: The Solow Building (9 West 57th Street) is a Midtown Manhattan skyscraper completed in 1974, designed by Gordon Bunshaft of SOM.
facts.quote: The Solow Building, also known as 9 West 57th Street, is a skyscraper in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City. Completed in 1974 and designed by Gordon Bunshaft of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, it is west of Fifth Avenue between 57th and 58th Streets, overlooking the Plaza Hotel and Central Park.

facts.fact: It is 210 metres tall with 50 storeys.
facts.quote: The building measures 689 feet (210 m) tall with 50 stories.

facts.fact: Its north and south facades curve inward from the ground to the 18th floor, then rise straight to the top.
facts.quote: The Solow Building's north and south facades curve inward from ground level to the 18th floor, where the tower rises upward to the 50th story.

facts.fact: It was the first major New York building developed with a sloped facade.
facts.quote: 9 West 57th Street was the first major structure in New York City to be developed with a sloped facade.

facts.fact: Bunshaft used curved facades instead of rectangular setbacks.
facts.quote: Bunshaft instead decided to use curved facades on the north and south elevations, avoiding the need for rectangular setbacks.

facts.fact: The north and south walls are grey-tinted glass; the west and east are clad in travertine.
facts.quote: The north and south walls are made of gray-tinted glass, while the west and east facades are clad in travertine.

facts.fact: On the travertine-clad ends, steel bracing crosses diagonally in front of narrow windows.
facts.quote: On either side is a narrow window opening spanning several stories. The building's structural steel bracing crosses diagonally in front of these windows.

facts.fact: Critics largely disliked it at first, seeing it as disruptive on the skyline.
facts.quote: The design was largely criticized upon the building's completion, with many architectural critics regarding the building as a disruptive presence on the skyline.

facts.fact: The Kunsthalle Bielefeld is a modern and contemporary art museum in Bielefeld, designed by Philip Johnson in 1968.
facts.quote: The Kunsthalle Bielefeld is a modern and contemporary art museum in Bielefeld, Germany. It was designed by Philip Johnson in 1968, and paid for by the businessman, art patron, and former Waffen-SS officer Rudolf August Oetker.

facts.fact: Built in the International Style, it is Johnson's only museum in Europe.
facts.quote: It was built in 1968 by the American architect Philip Johnson in the International Style that he had founded, and is his only museum building in Europe.

facts.fact: It is cubic with a square ground floor, three storeys above ground and two below, and 1,200 m² of galleries.
facts.quote: Cubic in shape and with a square ground level, it has three storeys above ground, two below, and a total exhibition space of 1,200 square metres (13,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: The facade is red sandstone.
facts.quote: The facade is of red sandstone.

facts.fact: It stands in a sculpture garden with works by Rodin, Henry Moore, Richard Serra and others.
facts.quote: The museum stands in a sculpture garden featuring works by Auguste Rodin, Henry Moore, Richard Serra, Thomas Schütte, Ólafur Elíasson and other modern sculptors.

facts.fact: Extensions proposed by Frank Gehry (1994) and Sou Fujimoto (2013) were never built.
facts.quote: Frank O. Gehry (1994) and Sou Fujimoto (2013) each proposed extensions to the existing building; none of them were realized.

facts.fact: Caruso St John was chosen in 2024 for a full renovation.
facts.quote: In 2022, Bielefeld's City Council decided in favour of a comprehensive renovation of the Kunsthalle Bielefeld, with a budget of 40.5 million euros. By 2024, architecture firm Caruso St John was selected ahead of 44 other submissions.

facts.fact: The Javits Center is a large convention center on Eleventh Avenue in Manhattan, designed by James Ingo Freed of Pei Cobb Freed & Partners.
facts.quote: The Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, commonly known as the Javits Center, is a large convention center on Eleventh Avenue between 34th Street and 38th Street in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan, New York City. It was designed by architect James Ingo Freed of Pei Cobb Freed & Partners.

facts.fact: The space frame structure was built from 1979 to 1986 and named after Senator Jacob Javits.
facts.quote: The space frame structure was constructed from 1979 to 1986 and was named to honor Jacob Javits, the United States senator for New York.

facts.fact: It replaced the New York Coliseum as the city's main convention hall.
facts.quote: When the Javits Center opened, it replaced the New York Coliseum at Columbus Circle as the city's major convention facility; the Coliseum was subsequently demolished and replaced by Time Warner Center.

facts.fact: Renovation brought a more transparent curtain wall, clearer skylights and light grey paint on the space frame.
facts.quote: The more transparent curtain wall, less opaque skylight systems, and light gray paint on the space frame have dramatically transformed the voluminous public spaces.

facts.fact: The new facade module went from 5 by 5 feet to 5 by 10 feet, allowing more transparent glass.
facts.quote: A new high-performance curtain wall has simplified and lightened the aesthetics of the original façade by changing the façade's module from 5 by 5 feet (1.5 m × 1.5 m) to 5 by 10 feet (1.5 m × 3.0 m).

facts.fact: Its roof became a 6.75-acre sedum green roof, the second-largest of its kind in the US.
facts.quote: The roof of the new expansion was turned into a 6.75-acre sedum green roof, making it the second-largest extensive green roof in the U.S.

facts.fact: An expansion finished in 2021 added 1.2 million square feet.
facts.quote: It has undergone expansions throughout its history, with the most recent expansion being completed in 2021 and adding 1.2 million square feet to the building.

facts.fact: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum is an art museum in Boston with European, Asian and American art.
facts.quote: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum is an art museum in Boston, Massachusetts, which houses significant examples of European, Asian, and American art.

facts.fact: It was built in 1898–1901 in the style of a 15th-century Venetian palace and opened in 1903.
facts.quote: The museum was built in 1898–1901 by Isabella Stewart Gardner (1840–1924), an American art collector, philanthropist, and patron of the arts in the style of a 15th-century Venetian palace. It opened to the public in 1903.

facts.fact: Gardner was so involved in the design that architect Willard T. Sears joked he was merely the structural engineer.
facts.quote: Gardner was deeply involved in every aspect of the design, leading Sears to quip that he was merely the structural engineer making Gardner's design possible.

facts.fact: Three floors of galleries surround a garden courtyard with a Roman mosaic.
facts.quote: Inside the museum, three floors of galleries surround a garden courtyard adorned with Roman mosaic, blooming with life in all seasons.

facts.fact: It was built new in Boston, but reuses many elements taken from Gothic and Renaissance buildings in Europe.
facts.quote: It was built from the ground up in Boston out of new materials, though it incorporates numerous architectural elements removed from European Gothic and Renaissance structures, worked into the design of the turn-of-the-century building.

facts.fact: The courtyard has a glass roof on its original steel structure.
facts.quote: The interior garden courtyard is covered by a glass roof, with steel support structure original to the building.

facts.fact: A new wing by Renzo Piano was completed in 2012.
facts.quote: An auxiliary wing designed by Italian architect Renzo Piano, adjacent to the original structure near the Back Bay Fens, was completed in 2012.

facts.fact: It is on the National Register of Historic Places (1983) and a Boston Landmark (2013).
facts.quote: In 1983, the museum was listed in the National Register of Historic Places. In 2013, the museum was designated a Boston Landmark by the Boston Landmarks Commission.

facts.fact: The Kyoto National Museum is one of Japan's major art museums, focused on pre-modern Japanese and Asian art.
facts.quote: The Kyoto National Museum (京都国立博物館, Kyōto Kokuritsu Hakubutsukan) is one of the major art museums in Japan. Located in Kyoto's Higashiyama ward, the museum focuses on pre-modern Japanese and Asian art.

facts.fact: It was proposed in 1889 as the Imperial Museum of Kyoto; construction finished in October 1895.
facts.quote: The Kyoto National Museum, then the Imperial Museum of Kyoto, was proposed, along with the Imperial Museum of Tokyo (Tokyo National Museum) and the Imperial Museum of Nara (Nara National Museum), in 1889, and construction on the museum finished in October 1895.

facts.fact: The museum opened in 1897.
facts.quote: The museum was opened in 1897.

facts.fact: Its best-known building is the Special Exhibition Hall, designed by Katayama Tōkuma in 1895.
facts.quote: The museum consists of several buildings, the most prominent being the Special Exhibition Hall (Main Exhibition Hall), designed by Katayama Tōkuma in 1895, and The Collections Hall (New Exhibition Hall), designed in 1966 by Morita Keiichi.

facts.fact: Katayama Tōkuma helped introduce Western, especially French, architecture into Japan.
facts.quote: Katayama Tōkuma (片山 東熊; 18 January 1854 – 24 October 1917) was a Japanese architect who designed the original buildings for the Imperial Nara Museum as well as the Kyoto Imperial Museum and was significant in introducing Western, particularly French architecture into Japan.

facts.fact: The Main Exhibition Hall, Main Gate and ticket area are Important Cultural Properties of Japan.
facts.quote: The Main Exhibition Hall, the Main Gate, and the Ticket Area have all been designated as Important Cultural Properties in Japan.

facts.fact: A new collections wing by Yoshio Taniguchi was completed in 2014.
facts.quote: In September 2014, the museum completed renovations on a new permanent collections hall, the Heisei Chishinkan Wing (The Collections Galleries), designed by Yoshio Taniguchi, known for his redesign of the Museum of Modern Art in New York and his design of the Gallery of Hōryū-ji Treasures at the Tokyo National Museum.

facts.fact: The Kobe Port Tower is a sightseeing tower and landmark in the port city of Kobe.
facts.quote: The Kobe Port Tower (神戸ポートタワー, Kōbe Pōto Tawā) is a landmark in the port city of Kobe, Japan.

facts.fact: It was designed by Nikken Sekkei and completed in 1963.
facts.quote: The Kobe Port Tower was designed by the Nikken Sekkei Company and was completed in 1963.

facts.fact: The 108-metre tower is shaped like a tsuzumi, a Japanese drum, and was the first tower built with a pipe lattice.
facts.quote: The Kobe Port Tower is 108 m (354 ft) high with a total of 8 layers that is designed to look like a Tsuzumi, a Japanese drum, and it is the first tower built using a pipe lattice.

facts.fact: It is ringed by 32 red steel staves.
facts.quote: The Tower is surrounded by 32 red steel staves as symbolize welcome vessels return to the shore.

facts.fact: The lowest viewing floor is 75 metres above the ground.
facts.quote: For the sightseeing layers, the first floor has aerial view from the viewing area as 75 m (250 ft) above the ground.

facts.fact: It closed in 2021 for renovation and seismic retrofitting and reopened in April 2024.
facts.quote: The facility was once again closed to the public from 27 September 2021 for renovation and seismic retrofitting. It reopened on 26 April 2024.

facts.fact: Kingdom Centre is a 99-storey, 302-metre skyscraper in Riyadh, the tallest in Saudi Arabia when completed in 2002.
facts.quote: Kingdom Centre (Arabic: مركز المملكة), formerly Kingdom Tower, is a 99-story, 302.3 m (992 ft) skyscraper in the al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. When completed in 2002, it overtook the 267-meter (876 ft) Faisaliah Tower as the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: Ellerbe Becket and Omrania were chosen through an international design competition.
facts.quote: The tower was developed by Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal, and designed by the team of Ellerbe Becket and Omrania, who were selected through an international design competition.

facts.fact: The upper third has an inverted parabolic arch topped by a public skybridge.
facts.quote: The upper third of the tower features an inverted parabolic arch topped by a public skybridge.

facts.fact: Its almond-shaped plan keeps it cool, with the narrow ends facing east and west where heat gain is greatest.
facts.quote: The tower's almond-shaped plan and curving forms gives the building a distinctive shape that helps keep it cool, with the narrow ends facing the east and west where heat gain is greatest.

facts.fact: The opening at the top let the building rise above the local limit of 30 occupied floors.
facts.quote: The large opening allows the building to rise higher than the height limit—30 occupied floors—mandated by local laws.

facts.fact: Its design drew on the Gateway Arch, the Sydney Harbour Bridge and the Eiffel Tower.
facts.quote: Its design was inspired by iconic structures from around the world, including the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, The Sydney Harbour Bridge, and the Eiffel Tower.

facts.fact: It is reinforced concrete for the first 180 metres and a tubular steel frame above.
facts.quote: Its structure consists of two systems: reinforced concrete columns, beams, and core for the first 180 meters, and a tubular steel frame structure for the building's remaining height.

facts.fact: It won the 2002 Emporis Skyscraper Award.
facts.quote: The Kingdom Centre is the winner of the 2002 Emporis Skyscraper Award, selected as the "best new skyscraper of the year for design and functionality".

facts.fact: The monument in Leipzig marks the 1813 Battle of the Nations and was completed in 1913, the battle's centenary.
facts.quote: The Monument to the Battle of the Nations (German: Völkerschlachtdenkmal) is a monument in Leipzig, Germany, to the 1813 Battle of Leipzig, also known as the Battle of the Nations. Paid for mostly by donations and the city of Leipzig, it was completed in 1913 for the 100th anniversary of the battle at a cost of six million gold marks.

facts.fact: Unconvinced by the competition winner, the organisers gave the commission to Bruno Schmitz, the most respected German architect of the time.
facts.quote: The Patriotic Association was again not convinced of the winning design and contemplated a third round, but in order not to lose more time, eventually decided to give the commission to Schmitz, who was the most well-respected German architect of the time.

facts.fact: It is built largely of concrete, faced with granite.
facts.quote: The structure makes extensive use of concrete, and the facings are of granite.

facts.fact: Schmitz built it on an artificial hill in a pyramidal shape; the base is 124 metres square.
facts.quote: Schmitz constructed the monument over an artificial hill and selected a pyramidal shape for a clear view of the surroundings. The base is 124 metres (407 ft) square.

facts.fact: It avoids classical elements and borrows from ancient Mesopotamian and Egyptian architecture.
facts.quote: Unlike many monuments and buildings of the era, the monument lacks classicist style elements, instead borrowing from the architecture of ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt.

facts.fact: In the round crypt, sixteen warrior statues stand guard as a symbolic tomb for the fallen.
facts.quote: In the circle-shaped crypt on the first floor, sixteen statues of warriors (Totenwächter) are present, symbolically standing guard, two each in front of a total of eight 6 m (6.6 yd) high death masks. The crypt was meant as a symbolic tomb for the fallen soldiers of the battle.

facts.fact: A 68-metre-high dome towers above the crypt.
facts.quote: Towering above the crypt is a 68 m (74 yd) high dome.

facts.fact: Of the planned ceremonial complex, only a reflecting pool and two processional avenues were built.
facts.quote: Schmitz also planned to create an accompanying complex for ceremonies that would include a court, a stadium and parade grounds. However, only a reflecting pool and two processional avenues were ultimately completed.

facts.fact: The National Museum of Finland in Helsinki presents Finnish history from the Stone Age to today.
facts.quote: The National Museum of Finland (Finnish: Suomen kansallismuseo, Swedish: Finlands Nationalmuseum) is a museum in Helsinki presenting Finnish history from the Stone Age to the present day, through objects and cultural history.

facts.fact: It was designed by the firm Gesellius, Lindgren, Saarinen.
facts.quote: The building of the National Museum was designed by the architect company Gesellius, Lindgren, Saarinen.

facts.fact: Its look reflects Finland's medieval churches and castles.
facts.quote: The appearance of the building reflects Finland's medieval churches and castles.

facts.fact: The architecture is National Romantic and the interior mainly Art Nouveau.
facts.quote: The architecture belongs to national romanticism and the interior mainly to Art Nouveau.

facts.fact: It was built from 1905 to 1910 and opened in 1916.
facts.quote: The museum was built from 1905 to 1910 and opened to the public in 1916.

facts.fact: The entrance hall ceiling has frescoes on Kalevala themes by Akseli Gallén-Kallela.
facts.quote: The museum's entrance hall ceiling has ceiling frescoes in the national epic Kalevala theme, painted by Akseli Gallén-Kallela, which can be seen without an entrance fee.

facts.fact: It is closed for renovation and expansion, expected to reopen in 2027.
facts.quote: The National Museum is currently closed due to a renovation and expansion project. The museum was estimated to reopen in 2027.

facts.fact: Wangjing SOHO is a complex of three curving, asymmetric office and retail towers in Beijing.
facts.quote: Wangjing SOHO (Chinese: 望京SOHO; pinyin: Wàngjīng SOHO) is a complex of three curvilinear asymmetric skyscrapers in Wangjing in Beijing, China, between central Beijing and Beijing Capital International Airport. The towers contain both office and retail space.

facts.fact: First planned as two towers, it was redesigned as three lower towers because of height concerns.
facts.quote: Originally the SOHO was designed as a two-tower complex but due to height concerns it was redesigned as a three-tower project featuring towers of lower maximum height.

facts.fact: It opened on 20 September 2014.
facts.quote: One of the more than a dozen properties developed by SOHO China, the complex officially opened on 20 September 2014.

facts.fact: It was designed by Zaha Hadid.
facts.quote: The structure was designed by Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid.

facts.fact: ArchDaily describes three curved towers whose shimmering metallic skin unifies them as they seem to dance around each other.
facts.quote: Architecture News Daily (Arch Daily) describes it as "three curved towers whose "shimmering", metallic skin unifies the complex as each volume appears to "dance" around each other."

facts.fact: The client said the design was meant to evoke koi, a Chinese symbol of wealth and luck.
facts.quote: Pan Shiyi, Chairman of the Board of SOHO China, said in an interview that the design of Wangjing SOHO was meant to evoke the image of Koi, a traditional Chinese symbol of wealth, luck, health and happiness.

facts.fact: Software was used to rationalise the facade's sheet-metal panels, meeting cost and manufacturing demands.
facts.quote: The software-driven panel-generation method was used to facilitate the rationalisation of manufactured sheet metal panels and to comply with higher demands in terms of cost requirements and manufacturing complexity.

facts.fact: John McArthur Jr. is best remembered as the architect of Philadelphia City Hall.
facts.quote: Best remembered as the architect of the landmark Philadelphia City Hall, McArthur also designed some of the city's most ambitious buildings of the Civil War era.

facts.fact: City Hall is in the Second Empire style; construction began in 1871.
facts.quote: In 1871, construction began on the Second Empire-style Philadelphia City Hall.

facts.fact: At 167 metres, its tower made it the world's tallest occupied building when completed.
facts.quote: Later, this was surpassed by the tower of City Hall (1874–1901), whose 548 feet (167 meters) made it the tallest occupied building in the world when completed.

facts.fact: Until the late 20th century, an unwritten rule kept Philadelphia buildings below the statue of William Penn on its tower.
facts.quote: Until the late 20th century, an unwritten agreement among Philadelphia architects kept all buildings shorter than the top of the statue of William Penn atop McArthur's tower.

facts.fact: It remained the city's tallest building until One Liberty Place in 1987.
facts.quote: The 548 ft (167 m) City Hall remained the tallest building in the city until 1987 when One Liberty Place was completed.

facts.fact: The Lipstick Building (885 Third Avenue) is a 138-metre, 34-floor office building in Midtown Manhattan, completed in 1986.
facts.quote: The Lipstick Building, also known as 885 Third Avenue and 53rd at Third, is a 453-foot-tall (138 m) office building at Third Avenue between 53rd Street and 54th Street in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City, New York, U.S. It was completed in 1986 and has 34 floors.

facts.fact: It was designed by John Burgee and Philip Johnson for Hines Interests.
facts.quote: The building was designed by John Burgee and Philip Johnson for Hines Interests and was developer Gerald D. Hines's first project in New York City.

facts.fact: Its nickname comes from its shape and colour, like a lipstick tube.
facts.quote: The building's nickname is derived from its shape and color, which resemble those of a lipstick tube.

facts.fact: It is nearly elliptical, with setbacks above the 19th and 27th storeys.
facts.quote: The building has a nearly elliptical massing, with setbacks above the 19th and 27th stories, as well as a two-story granite penthouse.

facts.fact: It is actually polygonal: each section has over a hundred sides.
facts.quote: The structure is actually polygonal; both the base and the setback sections have over a hundred sides.

facts.fact: It stands on double-height columns, with a facade of red Imperial granite and stainless steel.
facts.quote: The building stands on double-height columns at the base, and the facade is made of red Imperial granite and stainless steel.

facts.fact: The elliptical shape lets pedestrians cut across the corners and brings more light and air inside.
facts.quote: The elliptical shape allows pedestrians on 53rd and 54th Street to cut across the corners, and it permits additional light and air into the building.

facts.fact: A tube support system and central core brace it against the wind.
facts.quote: To brace the building against winds from the north, structural engineer Irwin Cantor designed a tube support system and a central core for the building's superstructure.

facts.fact: The Humboldt Forum is a museum of human history, art and culture inside the Berlin Palace on Museum Island in central Berlin.
facts.quote: The Humboldt Forum is a museum dedicated to human history, art and culture, located in the Berlin Palace on the Museum Island in the historic centre of Berlin.

facts.fact: It houses the non-European collections of the Berlin State Museums, along with temporary exhibitions and public events.
facts.quote: Considered the "German equivalent" of the British Museum, the Humboldt Forum houses the non-European collections of the Berlin State Museums, temporary exhibitions and public events.

facts.fact: The baroque palace that stood on the site was demolished in 1950 after heavy bomb damage in the Second World War.
facts.quote: The predominantly baroque historic building on this site had been demolished in 1950 by Walter Ulbricht of Socialist Unity Party of Germany (SED) following the massive damage during the bombing of Berlin in World War II.

facts.fact: Three facades from 1713, designed by Andreas Schlüter, were rebuilt along with Friedrich August Stüler's palace dome of 1853.
facts.quote: The three facades, which date back to 1713 and were designed by Andreas Schlüter, were reconstructed with the palace dome by Friedrich August Stüler from 1853.

facts.fact: Three baroque facades were rebuilt, while the passage through the palace forum and the east wing facing the Spree are a simple new design by the Italian architect Franco Stella.
facts.quote: For this purpose, three of the baroque facades were rebuilt, the palace forum as a passageway as well as the east wing facing the Spree River are a simple new creation by the Italian architect Franco Stella.

facts.fact: All the interiors are plain and functional, but were planned so they could be restored later.
facts.quote: All interiors are purely functional and simple in design, as is one side of the Schlüterhof. However, the interiors were planned to allow for later restoration.

facts.fact: The foundation stone was laid on 12 June 2013 and the shell was finished in June 2015.
facts.quote: The foundation stone was laid on 12 June 2013, and the shell was completed in June 2015.

facts.fact: Franco Stella's modernist Spree facade has been widely criticised.
facts.quote: In particular, the modernist Spree facade by architect Franco Stella has been widely criticized.
